must_remember: The Michelson Interferometer works on the principle of division of amplitude, splitting an incoming light beam into two mutually perpendicular paths using a beam splitter.
Circular fringes (Haidinger fringes) are formed when the mirrors are strictly parallel and correspond to fringes of equal inclination.
Localized fringes are formed when the mirrors are inclined at an angle, creating an air wedge between one mirror and the virtual image of the other.
A compensator plate of identical thickness and material is essential in white light interferometry to equalize the optical path in glass for both arms.
The path difference for oblique incidence is given by $\Delta = 2d \cos\theta$, where $d$ is the thickness of the air film and $\theta$ is the angle of incidence.

glossary.meaning: A partially silvered glass plate used to divide the amplitude of an incoming light beam into two perpendicular paths.
Circular fringes formed by equal inclination when the reflecting mirrors are strictly parallel.
A plate identical in thickness and material to the beam splitter, placed in the transmitted arm to equalize glass optical paths for white light interferometry.
The angle $\theta_w$ between inclined mirrors used to produce localized fringes.
A phase shift of $\pi$ radians (or $180^\circ$) experienced by light when reflected from an optically denser medium.
